consensus_summary: Consensus treats ‘virgin’ symbolically as purity, chastity, and exclusive covenant faithfulness to God, chiefly the Church or Israel as the pure bride betrothed to Christ/God, with secondary Marian, ascetic, readiness, and personified-nation uses.
book_summary: Book defines virgin as the espoused/betrothed to one husband with the wedding still ahead: covenant standing, not attainment; a betrothed virgin already counts as wife, the re-espoused ten-tribe house is called ‘virgin of Israel,’ and plural virgins are the bride’s companions; opposite is Harlot.
consensus_core_identification: Spiritual purity / exclusive fidelity embodied in the pure virgin-bride (Church or Israel).
book_core_identification: The espoused/betrothed one (covenant standing of betrothal with wedding still ahead).
boundary_disagreement: Book restricts the symbol to betrothal/covenant status (‘not attainment’) and explicitly includes the re-espoused divorced house and companion virgins, while treating harlot as the direct opposite; consensus centers moral/spiritual purity and admits broader purity, Marian, and ascetic cases without that status restriction.
material_contradiction: None on the shared bridal-covenant referent; the tension is only whether the core is purity-as-quality versus betrothal-as-standing.
rationale: Both identify the same bridal/covenant cluster (2 Cor 11:2, virgin Israel, Matt 25 companions). The book keeps that referent but materially re-precisifies it as legal-covenantal espousal status rather than purity attainment and reclassifies boundary cases (post-divorce re-espousal still ‘virgin’; plural companions; opposite = harlot), yielding refinement rather than equivalence or replacement.
strongest_objection: Consensus primary meaning is purity/chastity; reducing it to ‘covenant standing, not attainment’ may under-weight the moral-purity register attested across the same texts.
